overview.one_sentence: The Transformer replaces recurrent and convolutional layers in sequence transduction with pure attention mechanisms, enabling parallelization and achieving state-of-the-art translation performance with reduced training time.
overview.problem: Recurrent and convolutional neural networks in sequence transduction suffer from sequential computation bottlenecks, limiting parallelization and scalability, especially for long sequences and long-range dependencies.
overview.solution: A novel architecture called the Transformer uses stacked self-attention and position-wise feed-forward layers, eliminating recurrence and convolutions while enabling constant-time path lengths and full parallelization.
overview.why_it_matters: The Transformer achieves new state-of-the-art BLEU scores in machine translation (e.g., 28.4 on WMT 2014 English-to-German) while training 3–10× faster than prior models, demonstrating efficiency and scalability.

contributions.title: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
contributions.summary: Introduces a computationally efficient attention mechanism scaling dot-products by √dk to stabilize softmax gradients, enabling stable training with high-dimensional queries/keys.
contributions.importance: Replaces slower additive attention while maintaining performance, reducing memory/CPU overhead for large-scale training.

contributions.title: Multi-Head Attention
contributions.summary: Parallelizes attention across h=8 subspaces (d_k=d_v=d_model/h=64), allowing the model to attend to different representation types simultaneously without increasing computational cost.
contributions.importance: Mitigates information loss from single-head averaging by enabling diverse attention patterns (e.g., syntactic vs. semantic alignment).

contributions.title: Positional Encoding via Sinusoids
contributions.summary: Injects absolute/relative positional information using learned sinusoidal functions with geometrically spaced wavelengths, enabling generalization to unseen sequence lengths.
contributions.importance: Avoids learned embeddings’ limitations (fixed vocabulary size) while outperforming them empirically with minimal architectural overhead.

contributions.title: Full Parallelization via Self-Attention
contributions.summary: Eliminates sequential dependencies by replacing RNNs/convolutions with attention, enabling O(1) path length for long-range dependencies and full batch parallelism.
contributions.importance: Reduces training time from days/weeks to hours/days while improving translation quality (e.g., 28.4 BLEU vs. prior SOTA).

contributions.title: Generalization to Non-Translation Tasks
contributions.summary: Demonstrates strong performance on English constituency parsing (92.7 F1 in semi-supervised setting) with minimal task-specific tuning, showcasing attention’s versatility.
contributions.importance: Validates Transformer’s applicability beyond translation, opening avenues for multimodal and structured prediction tasks.

key_findings.title: WMT 2014 English-to-German Translation
key_findings.summary: Transformer (big) achieves new SOTA BLEU score surpassing all prior models (including ensembles) with 3.5 days of training on 8 P100 GPUs.

key_findings.title: WMT 2014 English-to-French Translation
key_findings.summary: Transformer (big) sets new single-model SOTA BLEU with 1/4 the training cost of prior best models, trained in 3.5 days on 8 GPUs.

key_findings.title: Training Efficiency vs. Prior Models
key_findings.summary: Transformer (base) achieves 27.3 BLEU in 12 hours (100K steps) on 8 GPUs, requiring 3–10× fewer FLOPs than competitive models (e.g., 3.3×10¹⁸ vs. 7.7×10¹⁹ for ConvS2S).

key_findings.title: Constituency Parsing Performance
key_findings.summary: 4-layer Transformer (d_model=1024) achieves 92.7 F1 in semi-supervised English parsing, outperforming prior SOTA (92.1) with no task-specific tuning.

limitations.title: Quadratic Memory Complexity
limitations.summary: Self-attention requires O(N²) memory for sequence length N, limiting batch size and sequence length due to GPU memory constraints.
limitations.details: Restricted attention (e.g., local windows) or sparse matrices may be needed for very long sequences (e.g., documents >1024 tokens).

limitations.title: Computational Overhead for Long Sequences
limitations.summary: Self-attention’s O(N²d) complexity per layer becomes prohibitive for N > 1024, unlike convolutions (O(kNd) with k < N).
limitations.details: Future work may explore sparse or hierarchical attention to mitigate this scaling issue.

limitations.title: Hyperparameter Sensitivity
limitations.summary: Performance degrades with suboptimal attention heads (e.g., single-head: 24.9 BLEU vs. 25.8 BLEU with 8 heads) or key dimensions (e.g., d_k=32: 25.3 BLEU).
limitations.details: Requires careful tuning of h and d_k/d_v for optimal compatibility function design.

limitations.title: Limited Evaluation on Non-Text Modalities
limitations.summary: Transformer’s applicability to audio/video/image tasks remains unexplored, despite its potential for parallelizing long-range dependencies in these domains.
limitations.details: Authors plan future work on extending attention to non-text modalities but did not provide empirical results.

equations.title: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
equations.explanation: This formula computes attention weights by taking the dot product of query vectors (Q) and key vectors (K), scaling them by the square root of the key dimension (d_k), applying a softmax function to obtain normalized weights, and then multiplying these weights with value vectors (V) to produce a weighted sum output.

variables.meaning: A matrix of query vectors derived from the input sequence, used to compute compatibility scores with keys.

variables.name: Key Matrix
variables.meaning: A matrix of key vectors derived from the input sequence, used to compute compatibility scores with queries.

variables.name: Value Matrix
variables.meaning: A matrix of value vectors, used to compute the weighted sum of values based on attention weights.

variables.name: Key Dimension
variables.meaning: The dimensionality of the key vectors, used for scaling the dot products to prevent gradient issues.

equations.latex: MultiHead(Q, K, V) = Concat\left(head_1, ..., head_h\right)W^O \quad \text{where} \quad head_i = Attention(QW_i^Q, KW_i^K, VW_i^V)
equations.explanation: This formula describes how multi-head attention works by linearly projecting the queries, keys, and values into multiple sets of vectors (h heads), computing attention for each set, concatenating the results, and then projecting them back to the original dimensionality using a learned weight matrix (W^O).

code_snippets.title: transformer_block.py
code_snippets.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import math

class MultiHeadAttention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model, num_heads):
        super().__init__()
        assert d_model % num_heads == 0, "d_model must be divisible by num_heads"
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.num_heads = num_heads
        self.d_k = d_model // num_heads

        self.W_q = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        self.W_k = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        self.W_v = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        self.W_o = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)

    def scaled_dot_product_attention(self, Q, K, V, mask=None):
        attn_scores = torch.matmul(Q, K.transpose(-2, -1)) / math.sqrt(self.d_k)
        if mask is not None:
            attn_scores = attn_scores.masked_fill(mask == 0, -1e9)
        attn_probs = torch.softmax(attn_scores, dim=-1)
        return torch.matmul(attn_probs, V), attn_probs

    def forward(self, Q, K, V, mask=None):
        Q = self.W_q(Q).view(Q.size(0), Q.size(1), self.num_heads, self.d_k).transpose(1, 2)
        K = self.W_k(K).view(K.size(0), K.size(1), self.num_heads, self.d_k).transpose(1, 2)
        V = self.W_v(V).view(V.size(0), V.size(1), self.num_heads, self.d_k).transpose(1, 2)

        attn_output, _ = self.scaled_dot_product_attention(Q, K, V, mask)
        attn_output = attn_output.transpose(1, 2).contiguous().view(attn_output.size(0), -1)
        return self.W_o(attn_output)

class PositionWiseFeedForward(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model, d_ff):
        super().__init__()
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(d_model, d_ff)
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(d_ff, d_model)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(0.1)

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.fc2(self.dropout(torch.relu(self.fc1(x))))

class EncoderBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model, num_heads, d_ff, dropout=0.1):
        super().__init__()
        self.attention = MultiHeadAttention(d_model, num_heads)
        self.feed_forward = PositionWiseFeedForward(d_model, d_ff)
        self.norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)

    def forward(self, x, mask=None):
        attn_output = self.attention(x, x, x, mask)
        x = self.norm1(x + self.dropout(attn_output))
        ff_output = self.feed_forward(x)
        return self.norm2(x + self.dropout(ff_output))

metadata.title: Attention Is All You Need
metadata.abstract: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder. The best performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train. Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including ensembles, by over 2 BLEU. On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of the best models from the literature. We show that the Transformer generalizes well to other tasks by applying it successfully to English constituency parsing both with large and limited training data.
